evidence.quote: In the specimen after multiaxial forging, a higher amount of fine dynamic recrystallized grains has been observed and the dynamic recrystallization (DRX) has occurred more severely and thoroughly compared to those after UAF, as depicted in Fig. 5 (d).

As shown in Figs. 4 and 5, a higher amount of DRX grains can be observed in the specimen after multiaxial forging (MAF) than the one after uniaxial forging (UAF), indicating that the DRX occurs more severely and thoroughly during MAF.
After MAF, the grains are extremely refined by DRX to increase the amount of grain boundaries.
Therefore, the increased yield strength of the multiaxial forged specimen can be explained by the refined grain size.

Meanwhile, the contribution from grain boundary sliding becomes important during high temperature deformation, and the fine equiaxed grains can promote grain sliding and relieve stress concentration, so that the deformation can be conducted more uniformly and coordinately, which is conducive to the increase in elongation and even realization of superplasticity.
As the forging proceeds to a certain extent, the dynamic recrystallization (DRX) could be activated by high density of dislocations, mechanical twins and α2/γ lamellar decomposition.
